emb:L2039868854.clinical_problem: nuchal translucency measurement and screening for fetal abnormality
emb:L2039868854.patient_population: fetuses undergoing first-trimester nuchal translucency ultrasound; retrospective images used to train ultrasound resident sonographers
emb:L2039868854.model_description: An AI model automatically identifies the nuchal translucency (NT) plane on fetal ultrasound images and measures NT thickness. In this study it was used as a training aid: after an initial round of independent NT identification, measurement and diagnosis, two resident sonographers received additional AI-assisted training, then all sonographers performed a second independent round that was compared to a fetal medicine expert's blinded review. The AI model itself was not the subject of an accuracy evaluation here, only its effect on trainee performance.
emb:L2039868854.headline_result: AI-assisted training significantly improved NT measurement standardization rate in both resident sonographers (chi2=25.768 and 17.035, both P<0.05) and diagnostic accuracy in one resident (chi2=10.180, P<0.05); traditional lecture-only training produced no significant improvement in the middle-age sonographer

emb:L2039869139.exclusion_reason: adult gynecologic ultrasound (uterine fibroids), not a pediatric population

emb:L2039763472.model_family: machine learning and deep learning models (various, pooled across included studies)
emb:L2039763472.clinical_problem: pediatric brain tumor diagnosis (tumor type, molecular subtype) and prognosis (survival)
emb:L2039763472.patient_population: pediatric patients with brain cancer imaged with MRI, pooled across included studies
emb:L2039763472.model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of machine learning and deep learning models applied to MRI in pediatric brain cancer. Included studies used ML/DL to predict tumor type (e.g., distinguishing pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma), molecular markers (e.g., BRAF mutation/fusion in low-grade glioma), or prognosis (overall, progression-free, or event-free survival). Reporting quality was assessed with TRIPOD+AI and risk of bias with PROBAST+AI.
emb:L2039763472.headline_result: Among low-risk-of-bias studies, median AUC 0.85 (IQR 0.82-0.94) for diagnostic models and 0.88 (IQR 0.86-0.89) for prognostic models; no consistent trend of deep learning outperforming machine learning or of models outperforming clinical experts

emb:L2039953412.exclusion_reason: methodological fMRI connectivity-analysis technique (functional covariance modes), not an AI/ML diagnostic model applied to clinical radiology

emb:L2039953474.exclusion_reason: animal (mouse) model study, not a human pediatric population

emb:L2039912979.model_family: dropout-trained nnU-Net (3D CNN) with modality-dropout training, compared to generative image synthesis and heuristic imputation
emb:L2039912979.clinical_problem: pediatric brain tumor segmentation and prognosis when MRI sequences are missing from the exam
emb:L2039912979.patient_population: children with pediatric brain tumors: 715 patients from the Children's Brain Tumor Network and BraTS-PEDs, plus 43 patients with longitudinal MRI from PNOC003/007 clinical trials
emb:L2039912979.model_description: An nnU-Net tumor segmentation model was trained with random dropout of FLAIR and/or non-contrast T1-weighted sequences to simulate incomplete pediatric brain tumor MRI exams. It was compared against a generative image-synthesis model and simple copy-substitution/zeroing heuristics for handling missing sequences. Tumor volumes from each method fed into time-varying Cox regression models to estimate survival risk.
emb:L2039912979.dataset_size: 715 patients (CBTN and BraTS-PEDs) plus 43 patients with 157 longitudinal MRI timepoints (PNOC003/007)
emb:L2039912979.headline_result: Dropout-trained segmentation model showed only up to 0.04 Dice drop under missing MRI and a stable survival C-index of 0.65 versus complete-input performance; image synthesis achieved SSIM > 0.90
emb:L2039912979.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional cohort study, technical development

emb:L2039580886.exclusion_reason: MRI-to-CT image synthesis method developed and evaluated primarily on adult datasets (SynthRAD2023, IXI, BraTS2024, CT-ich); pediatric performance mentioned only in passing without population details

emb:L2039581149.exclusion_reason: fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES), an endoscopic modality, not radiologic imaging

emb:L2039912845.exclusion_reason: survey study of pediatric emergency staff attitudes toward ML decision support, not an imaging AI model

emb:L2039950986.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience/psychiatric biomarker research using resting-state fMRI and SVR, not a clinical radiology diagnostic application

emb:L2039912571.model_family: various AI-assisted ultrasound diagnostic tools (pooled across reviewed studies)
emb:L2039912571.body_region: multiple fetal organ systems (heart, brain/cranial, face)
emb:L2039912571.clinical_problem: prenatal detection and classification of congenital anomalies on ultrasound
emb:L2039912571.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound screening for congenital anomalies, pooled across 20 included studies
emb:L2039912571.model_description: A systematic review of AI-assisted ultrasound diagnostic tools used to detect fetal congenital anomalies during pregnancy. Most reviewed studies focused on single-organ detection (heart 35%, brain/cranial 30%, facial features 20%), with fewer addressing multi-organ detection (15%). Studies were appraised using the CLAIM checklist for AI in medical imaging.
emb:L2039912571.dataset_size: 20 studies included (from 9,918 records screened, 224 full texts reviewed)
emb:L2039912571.headline_result: 50% of included studies reported both sensitivity and specificity exceeding 0.95, with AUC-ROC 0.91-0.97; 75% of studies lacked external validation

emb:L2036995633.model_name: AIM-NT (Automated Identification and Measurement of Nuchal Translucency)
emb:L2036995633.clinical_problem: nuchal translucency plane identification and thickness measurement for prenatal screening
emb:L2036995633.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound NT assessment, January 2022-October 2023, multicenter
emb:L2036995633.model_description: AIM-NT is a deep learning model that automatically identifies the correct nuchal translucency imaging plane on prenatal ultrasound and measures NT thickness in real time. It was developed and tested on an internal dataset, then evaluated on an external multicenter dataset, with plane identification accuracy, timing, and thickness measurements compared to those of experienced radiologists.
emb:L2036995633.dataset_size: internal: 3,959 NT images from 3,153 fetuses; external: 267 ultrasound videos from 267 fetuses
emb:L2036995633.headline_result: AUC 0.92 for NT plane identification on internal test set; external accuracy 88.8% (AIM-NT) vs 87.6% (radiologists), P=.69; mean NT measurement difference 0.03 mm, mean absolute error 0.22 mm

emb:L2037182637.clinical_problem: assessment of fetal neuromotor development via facial motor activity
emb:L2037182637.patient_population: 45 fetuses imaged with 4D ultrasound across five structured behavioral conditions
emb:L2037182637.model_description: A commercial AI facial-landmark-tracking engine (Visage|SDK), originally trained on postnatal imagery, was applied to 4D ultrasound video of fetal faces to track facial movements across five conditions (baseline, maternal voice, calming music, stimulating music, recovery). Frame-level tracking success fed into a five-point Fetal Behavioral Arousal Index (FBAI) summarizing facial motor activity intensity and frequency.
emb:L2037182637.release_evidence: a commercial AI engine (Visage|SDK) for facial landmark tracking
emb:L2037182637.headline_result: Estimated AI frame-level detection success averaged 70.4%; FBAI scores higher during verbal interaction and stimulating music than baseline/calming stimuli (P<0.05); moderate correlation between FBAI and fetal heart rate (r=0.52)

emb:L2037182807.clinical_problem: diagnostic value and clinical/ethical implications of AI-enhanced ultrasound image rendering
emb:L2037182807.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound, in the context of commercially marketed AI-enhanced imaging
emb:L2037182807.model_description: A narrative integrative review critically evaluates AI-enhanced '8K' fetal ultrasound image rendering, a commercially marketed technology that algorithmically enhances standard 3D ultrasound images for greater visual clarity. The review synthesizes image-quality comparisons between standard 3D ultrasound and AI-enhanced renderings but does not develop a new model itself.
emb:L2037182807.release_evidence: AI-enhanced 8K fetal ultrasound imaging, a rapidly emerging technology marketed as a breakthrough in prenatal diagnostics
emb:L2037182807.headline_result: No peer-reviewed studies demonstrated enhanced diagnostic accuracy, anomaly detection, or improved perinatal outcomes from AI-enhanced 8K imaging, despite improved perceived visual clarity

emb:L2038562159.exclusion_reason: review of sandplay psychotherapy; not radiologic imaging

emb:L2039480732.model_name: NRDLS (Novel Real-time Deep Learning method for Ultrasound Screening)
emb:L2039480732.model_family: ensemble deep learning model with transfer learning; two-stage detection and classification
emb:L2039480732.clinical_problem: screening and diagnosis of biliary atresia via gallbladder localization ('ghost gallbladder') in prenatal and neonatal jaundice
emb:L2039480732.patient_population: neonates aged 25-77 days with obstructive jaundice at first diagnosis; also addresses prenatal fetal gallbladder screening
emb:L2039480732.model_description: NRDLS is a two-stage deep learning system that localizes the fetal or neonatal gallbladder (including difficult-to-find 'ghost' gallbladders) on ultrasound and then classifies the images to diagnose biliary atresia. It was built via transfer learning from an ensemble deep learning model and evaluated on data from hospitals different from the training site, then deployed for frontline screening in several primary care hospitals.
emb:L2039480732.dataset_size: derivation cohort from Guangzhou Women and Children Medical Center PACS records, 2010-2024; external validation cohorts of 118 and 72 patients with neonatal jaundice
emb:L2039480732.headline_result: Detection mean average precision 92.8%, AUC 0.917-0.944; external validation AUC 82% and 85%; after deployment, novice physicians achieved mean AUC 0.92, specificity 0.93, F1-score 0.83
emb:L2039480732.study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study with prospective clinical deployment

emb:L2039419574.model_description: Two ResNet-50 models pretrained on different source datasets - ImageNet (14 million natural images) versus RadImageNet (1.4 million medical images) - were fine-tuned to detect pneumonia on chest X-rays of children aged 1-5 years. Performance was compared across six evaluation metrics to test whether a medically pretrained backbone improves classification on a small pediatric imaging dataset.
emb:L2039419574.dataset_size: not stated precisely (chest X-ray images of children aged 1-5)
emb:L2039419574.headline_result: RadImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 outperformed ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 across six evaluation metrics for pediatric pneumonia detection

emb:L2039468537.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray dataset population not explicitly stated as pediatric; children mentioned only as general disease-burden background

emb:L2039468302.clinical_problem: fetal lung volume and lobar segmentation for prediction of neonatal outcomes, including congenital diaphragmatic hernia
emb:L2039468302.patient_population: 104 normal-anatomy fetal controls and 45 congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases; 290 controls used for growth charts, across 0.55T, 1.5T and 3T scanners
emb:L2039468302.model_description: A 3D Attention U-Net automatically segments the fetal lungs into five standard lobes on 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal body MRI, replacing time-consuming manual 2D slice-by-slice segmentation. It was trained on normal-anatomy and congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases across 0.55T, 1.5T and 3T scanners, and used to generate normal fetal lung volumetry growth charts.
emb:L2039468302.dataset_size: 104 normal controls and 45 CDH cases for the training dataset; 18 cases for evaluation; 290 controls for growth charts
emb:L2039468302.headline_result: Good Dice performance for normal lung anatomy on 18 evaluation cases, with expectedly lower Dice values for the ipsilateral lung in congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases

emb:L2039332299.model_name: GSCAViT (grouped sharing convolutional attention - vision transformer)
emb:L2039332299.model_family: vision transformer with denoising group-sharing convolutional attention module
emb:L2039332299.clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal echocardiographic views
emb:L2039332299.model_description: GSCAViT is a deep learning model that classifies seven standard fetal echocardiogram view types (e.g., three-vessel and trachea, four-chamber, aortic arch, bicaval, outflow tracts) from ultrasound images. It combines a denoising group-sharing convolutional attention module with a vision transformer, and uses SHAP explainability to visualize which image features drive classification.
emb:L2039332299.headline_result: Accuracy 97.1%, precision 97.1%, recall 97.0%, F1-score 97.0% in validation; AUCs of 0.994, 0.928, and 0.932 on three separate test sets

emb:L2039444619.model_family: AI-assisted bone age assessment (architecture not stated), applied to three established prediction formulas (Bayley-Pinneau, Tanner-Whitehouse 3, China 05)
emb:L2039444619.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment for adult height prediction in girls with pubertal disorders
emb:L2039444619.patient_population: 278 female children undergoing pubertal development assessment at Shenzhen Children's Hospital, 2014-2020, followed until adult height was reached
emb:L2039444619.model_description: AI-assisted bone age assessment of left-hand-wrist radiographs was used to apply three adult-height prediction methods (Bayley-Pinneau, Tanner-Whitehouse 3, and China 05) in girls followed to adult height, comparing which method most accurately predicted final adult height and how errors varied by age, bone age delay/advancement, and pubertal stage.
emb:L2039444619.headline_result: TW3 and BP methods overestimated adult height by 2.6+-3.0 cm and 1.7+-3.7 cm; China 05 underestimated by 2.3+-3.5 cm; proportion of predictions within +-5 cm of final height: TW3 80.0%, BP 77.0%, China 05 74.2% (P=0.038)

emb:L2039719240.exclusion_reason: functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) hyperscanning study; not a diagnostic radiologic imaging modality

emb:L2037746491.model_family: attention module combined with existing CNN and transformer-based segmentation models
emb:L2037746491.body_region: whole body (bone scan), chest, and brain across different experiments
emb:L2037746491.clinical_problem: segmentation of lesions in noisy nuclear medicine images and other medical images, leveraging anatomical symmetry
emb:L2037746491.patient_population: adolescents undergoing whole-body bone scans, among other imaging cohorts used to validate the general method
emb:L2037746491.model_description: Deformable Symmetry Attention (DSA) is an attention module that exploits left-right anatomical symmetry to improve automated lesion segmentation on grainy nuclear medicine images. It reflects the image to leverage symmetry, applies deformable registration to correct local anatomical variation, and redistributes attention with learnable Gaussian kernels to address pixel-level noise. It was combined with CNN and transformer segmentation models and tested on several tasks, including lesion segmentation on adolescent whole-body bone scans, 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation, and chest X-ray anatomical segmentation.
emb:L2037746491.headline_result: 3.8% to 8.48% Dice improvement segmenting lesions in adolescent whole-body bone scans; 2.88% improvement in 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation; 0.63% to 10.57% improvement in chest X-ray anatomical segmentation

emb:L2039116433.exclusion_reason: bibliometric analysis of the AI-in-obstetric-imaging literature, not a study of an AI model

emb:L2039104984.exclusion_reason: imaging of the maternal cervix to predict preterm birth risk; not fetal or pediatric anatomy

emb:L2039105212.exclusion_reason: general lifespan brain-aging classification study using resting-state fMRI; pediatric-specific population not established in the abstract

emb:L2037671087.model_name: FNB-ADS (Fetal Nasal Bone development Automated Diagnostic System)
emb:L2037671087.model_family: cascaded pipeline: YOLOv8 detection, lightweight segmentation network, ResNet34 classification
emb:L2037671087.clinical_problem: prenatal screening for chromosomal abnormality via fetal nasal bone development assessment
emb:L2037671087.patient_population: fetuses undergoing early-pregnancy mid-sagittal ultrasound screening
emb:L2037671087.model_description: FNB-ADS is a cascaded deep learning pipeline for early prenatal fetal nasal bone (FNB) screening: YOLOv8 localizes the FNB region on mid-sagittal ultrasound images, a lightweight network segments the nasal bone, tip, and prenasal skin, and a ResNet34 classifier diagnoses developmental abnormalities. The authors also released a public image and video dataset (FNB-UDV) for this task.
emb:L2037671087.release_evidence: The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/SIGMACX/FNB-AD/tree/FNB-ADS
emb:L2037671087.dataset_size: 1,007 two-dimensional ultrasound images and 12 ultrasound videos (FNB-UDV dataset)
emb:L2037671087.headline_result: Image diagnostic accuracy 92.37% with 0.14 s per-image processing time; video diagnostic accuracy 98.69% with 0.37 s per-frame inference speed

emb:L2039066793.exclusion_reason: population age range not stated (ABIDE II database spans children through adults); pediatric-specific cohort not established in the abstract

emb:L2039467407.exclusion_reason: non-imaging clinical trial biomarker/phenotype classification, not a radiologic imaging AI model

emb:L2030837794.patient_population: children whose chest X-rays make up the public Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre pneumonia dataset
emb:L2030837794.model_description: ConvMixer replaces standard convolutional layers with a mixer that separately processes channel and spatial information, reducing the number of parameters and computations per layer. It was applied to a large, publicly available set of pediatric chest X-rays from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre (via Kaggle) to classify images as normal or pneumonia.
emb:L2030837794.dataset_size: large numbers of chest X-ray images, publicly available on Kaggle (Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre)
emb:L2030837794.headline_result: Highest accuracy 95.11%, also evaluated for precision, recall, and F1-score

emb:L2033079723.model_family: multi-task learning with an improved Swin Transformer (spatial and channel reconstruction convolutional Swin block)
emb:L2033079723.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (Risser stage) assessment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis evaluation and treatment
emb:L2033079723.patient_population: adolescents with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing pelvis radiography
emb:L2033079723.model_description: A multi-task deep learning approach extracts the iliac region from pelvis radiographs and forwards it to an improved Swin Transformer to automatically grade Risser stage, a skeletal-maturity measure used in scoliosis evaluation and treatment, aiming to reduce inter- and intra-observer variability seen with manual grading. Grad-CAM visualization was used to interpret model predictions, and code was released on GitHub.
emb:L2033079723.headline_result: Overall accuracy 81.53% for Risser stage assessment, improving on ResNet50 (+5.85%), ResNet101 (+4.6%), Uni-former (+3.6%), Next-ViT (+2.7%), ConvNeXt (+2.25%), and the original Swin Transformer (+1.8%)

emb:L2037068960.model_family: U-Net variant with Zernike Attention, Wavelet Attention, and Morphological Constraint modules
emb:L2037068960.clinical_problem: assessment of fetal brain development via corpus callosum segmentation on prenatal ultrasound
emb:L2037068960.patient_population: fetuses at 18-32 weeks gestation undergoing brain ultrasound
emb:L2037068960.model_description: FB-ZWUNet is an end-to-end deep learning network that automatically segments the corpus callosum on mid-sagittal fetal brain ultrasound images, replacing manual segmentation. It combines a Zernike Attention Module for feature enhancement, a Wavelet Attention Module for feature fusion and reconstruction, and a Morphological Constraint Module for accurate edge and region capture, trained on the FB-CC dataset spanning 18-32 weeks gestation across three ultrasound devices.
emb:L2037068960.dataset_size: 1,336 annotated fetal brain mid-sagittal ultrasound images (FB-CC dataset)
emb:L2037068960.headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.8743, IoU 0.7813, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, stability, and inference speed

emb:L2037209722.model_family: multi-task deep learning model with ShuffleNetV2 backbone, CARAFE feature reassembly, and Coordinate Attention
emb:L2037209722.clinical_problem: detection and classification of fetal nasal bone defects (a chromosomal-abnormality marker) on prenatal ultrasound
emb:L2037209722.patient_population: 731 mid-pregnancy women undergoing fetal nasal bone ultrasound
emb:L2037209722.model_description: FNBUI-NET is a real-time multi-task deep learning model that detects and classifies the fetal nasal bone as normal, dysplastic, or absent on ultrasound images. It integrates a ShuffleNetV2 backbone with a content-aware feature reassembly module and coordinate attention for feature compression, balancing detection speed and accuracy. The authors also built the FNBUI dataset to support this task.
emb:L2037209722.dataset_size: 1,104 ultrasound images from 731 mid-pregnancy women (FNBUI dataset)
emb:L2037209722.headline_result: mAP@0.5 of 0.985 for nasal bone detection; classification accuracy 0.981, outperforming 18 existing methods

emb:L2039451014.model_family: various AI techniques reviewed (e.g., DW-Net, DGACNN, FINE, EchoNet-Dynamic)
emb:L2039451014.clinical_problem: prenatal and postnatal detection of congenital heart disease via echocardiography
emb:L2039451014.patient_population: fetuses and children undergoing echocardiography for congenital heart disease, pooled across 108 reviewed articles
emb:L2039451014.model_description: A narrative review of AI applications in fetal and pediatric transthoracic echocardiography for congenital heart disease, covering image recognition, auxiliary diagnosis, cardiac function measurement, and imaging quality control. It surveys named systems such as DW-Net, DGACNN, FINE, and EchoNet-Dynamic, discussing reported benefits for workflow and diagnostic accuracy alongside barriers to clinical adoption.

emb:L2039030539.clinical_problem: detection of subtle cortical lesions in pediatric focal epilepsy surgery evaluation
emb:L2039030539.patient_population: paediatric focal epilepsy patients (17 MRI-lesion-positive, 14 MRI-negative; 26 evaluable after exclusions), plus 10 healthy volunteers used for network training
emb:L2039030539.model_description: A 3D U-Net, trained on paired 3T and 7T MRI from 10 healthy volunteers, enhances quantitative R1 relaxation maps acquired at standard 3T field strength to approximate the image quality of ultra-high-field 7T MRI. It was applied to 3T R1 maps from a separate cohort of pediatric focal epilepsy patients scanned at a different site, and radiologists compared lesion visibility and detection on the AI-enhanced maps versus original 3T maps and 3D-FLAIR.
emb:L2039030539.dataset_size: 10 healthy volunteers for training; 17 MRI-positive and 14 MRI-negative pediatric epilepsy patients for application
emb:L2039030539.headline_result: Lesions detected on AI-enhanced R1 maps in 14/15 (93%) MR-positive and 4/11 (36%) MR-negative patients, with superior image quality compared to original 3T R1 maps and 3D-FLAIR
emb:L2039030539.study_design: retrospective technical development with radiological review

emb:L2039031402.exclusion_reason: panoramic dental radiograph diagnosis; dental imaging is excluded

emb:L2039217866.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience research on adolescent functional-connectome development and psychosocial factors, not a clinical radiology diagnostic AI application

emb:L2038821803.model_family: commercial computer-aided detection systems for chest X-ray: CAD4TB_v7, qXR_v4, InferRead DR Chest (InfV)
emb:L2038821803.clinical_problem: tuberculosis diagnosis in children via chest X-ray
emb:L2038821803.patient_population: children aged 0-14 years at two health facilities in Lusaka, Zambia, evaluated with Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and chest X-ray
emb:L2038821803.model_description: Three commercial computer-aided detection (CAD) systems for chest X-ray - CAD4TB_v7, qXR_v4, and InferRead DR Chest - were evaluated for their ability to identify TB-consistent findings on children's chest radiographs, compared against a microbiological reference standard (Xpert Ultra), a composite reference standard, and consensus reads by six expert human readers.
emb:L2038821803.release_evidence: 3 CAD systems (CAD4TB_v7, qxr_v4, and InferRead DR Chest (InfV))
emb:L2038821803.dataset_size: 609 children enrolled; 515 with corresponding GeneXpert Ultra results and CXR outcomes
emb:L2038821803.headline_result: Against the microbiological reference standard, CAD4TB_v7 AUC 0.75, qXR_v4 AUC 0.69, InfV AUC 0.54; against the expert-reader reference standard, CAD4TB_v7 AUC 0.81, qXR_v4 AUC 0.83, InfV AUC 0.63

emb:L2038788483.model_family: Geometric Morphometric Methods (GMM) with Elastic Net logistic regression (landmark-based, not deep learning)
emb:L2038788483.clinical_problem: non-invasive screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, aiming to reduce radiographic exposure
emb:L2038788483.patient_population: 168 individuals (135 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, 33 controls)
emb:L2038788483.model_description: Automatic landmark extraction from 3D torso surface scans is combined with geometric morphometric analysis and principal component analysis to derive shape variables, which are then classified with a regularized (Elastic Net) logistic regression model to detect adolescent idiopathic scoliosis without radiographs.
emb:L2038788483.headline_result: AUC 0.925, sensitivity 93%, specificity 86%, balanced accuracy 89% on an unseen test set

emb:L2039215469.clinical_problem: image-quality improvement for reconstructed fetal brain MRI to support prenatal neural disorder diagnosis
emb:L2039215469.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal brain MRI (simulated and in vivo data)
emb:L2039215469.model_description: PW-GAN is an unsupervised generative adversarial network that denoises 3D fetal brain MRI volumes reconstructed from motion-corrupted thick-slice scans. It treats denoising as an unpaired style-transfer problem between low- and high-quality MRI domains and adds a pseudo-deformation-field module, based on optical flow, to keep structures consistent between adjacent slices while removing residual noise and interpolation artifacts.
emb:L2039215469.dataset_size: not stated precisely (simulated and in vivo data)
emb:L2039215469.headline_result: Outperforms existing unsupervised denoising models and achieves performance on par with several state-of-the-art supervised methods

emb:L2039030569.exclusion_reason: machine learning applied to serum iron biomarkers to predict carotid intima-media thickness; not an imaging-based AI model, and the population is predominantly adults with only a pediatric subgroup analysis

emb:L2036700115.model_family: modified U-Net with atrous spatial pyramid pooling and squeeze-and-excitation blocks; YOLOv5 for detection
emb:L2036700115.clinical_problem: fetal head circumference measurement on prenatal ultrasound
emb:L2036700115.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (public HC18 dataset)
emb:L2036700115.model_description: The pipeline first detects the fetal head using YOLOv5 with transfer learning, then segments it with SAP-UNet (a modified U-Net incorporating atrous spatial pyramid pooling and squeeze-and-excitation blocks), and finally fits an ellipse to the segmentation to automatically measure head circumference from 2D ultrasound images.
emb:L2036700115.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 98.02%+-0.8, Hausdorff distance 1.20+-0.68 mm, HC difference -0.08+-1.2 mm, HC absolute difference 1.11+-1.3 mm on the HC18 dataset

emb:L2036852468.exclusion_reason: phonocardiogram (auscultation audio) based AI, not a diagnostic imaging modality

emb:L2037429264.model_family: image-processing/segmentation pipeline with fast ellipse fitting; segmentation backbones compared included HRNet
emb:L2037429264.clinical_problem: fetal growth assessment via head circumference, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter measurement
emb:L2037429264.model_description: The algorithm takes a segmented fetal head ultrasound image, from any of several compared segmentation models, and applies a fast ellipse-fitting method to automatically compute head circumference, head orientation, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter. Three segmentation models were compared, with HRNet performing best, to demonstrate the approach's compatibility with different segmentation backbones.
emb:L2037429264.headline_result: HRNet segmentation backbone achieved the best average Dice score of 0.96 among the three compared models

emb:L2038506249.exclusion_reason: chest X-ray dataset population not explicitly stated as pediatric; children mentioned only as background context for disease burden

emb:L2038321162.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience research predicting alcohol-use trajectories from multimodal MRI in a general adolescent cohort (ABCD study), not a clinical radiology diagnostic application

emb:L2038275920.exclusion_reason: general review of ML/DL in ADHD diagnosis across multiple non-imaging domains (text, EEG, behavioral, genomics); not focused on radiologic imaging AI

emb:L2038622515.patient_population: pediatric brain tumor cases from the BraTS-PED 2024 dataset
emb:L2038622515.model_description: This study tests whether adding T1w/T2w ratio maps, a voxel-wise combination of T1- and T2-weighted MRI signal previously used to study cortical architecture, as extra input channels improves nnU-Net segmentation of pediatric brain tumor subregions on the BraTS-PED 2024 dataset.
emb:L2038622515.headline_result: T1w/T2w ratio maps did not improve nnU-Net segmentation performance for pediatric brain tumor subregions

emb:L2039212308.model_family: MLP-based, Transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based deep learning architectures (compared)
emb:L2039212308.clinical_problem: estimation of fiber orientation distributions from diffusion MRI to study early brain development, addressing generalizability across scanners and protocols
emb:L2039212308.patient_population: 488 infant subjects from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) and Baby Connectome Project (BCP)
emb:L2039212308.model_description: Three deep learning architectures (MLP-based, transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based) were trained to estimate fiber orientation distribution functions from infant diffusion MRI, and their robustness to domain shifts (scanner/protocol differences, age, number of input gradient directions) was systematically evaluated. Two adaptation strategies, method-of-moments and fine-tuning, were tested to correct inter-site domain shift, with fine-tuning giving the best results.
emb:L2039212308.headline_result: U-Net outperformed other models with fewer diffusion gradient directions; performance plateaued from 28-45 input directions across all models; fine-tuning outperformed method-of-moments for correcting inter-site domain shift

emb:L2038622318.model_family: various AI/ML algorithms reviewed (ensemble neural networks, CNN variants including YOLO and DenseNet, explainable AI)
emb:L2038622318.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart defects via fetal echocardiography
emb:L2038622318.patient_population: fetuses across gestational ages undergoing prenatal echocardiography, approximately 20,000 pregnancies across 40 reviewed studies
emb:L2038622318.model_description: A systematic review of 40 primary studies comparing AI/machine-learning algorithms (ensemble neural networks, CNN variants including YOLO and DenseNet, and explainable AI methods) against traditional fetal echocardiography for detecting congenital heart defects, summarizing sensitivity and specificity across gestational ages and defect types.
emb:L2038622318.headline_result: AI algorithms detected congenital heart defects with 95-96% accuracy versus 88-90% for traditional ultrasound methods; one report AUC 0.883 (AI) vs 0.749 (residents) and 0.808 (fellows)

emb:L2032606294.model_family: signal filtering combined with convolutional neural networks and U-Nets
emb:L2032606294.clinical_problem: assessment of hip displacement severity (migration percentage) in children with cerebral palsy
emb:L2032606294.patient_population: children with cerebral palsy undergoing hip ultrasound, 62 hips (coronal and transverse scans)
emb:L2032606294.model_description: A pipeline combining signal filtering, convolutional neural networks, and U-Nets segments the regions of interest and detects landmarks on hip ultrasound images to automatically compute migration percentage (MP), the standard measure of hip displacement severity in cerebral palsy, as a radiation-free alternative to the conventional X-ray-based measurement.
emb:L2032606294.dataset_size: 62 hips (36 used for training with augmentation, 8 for validation, 18 for testing)
emb:L2032606294.headline_result: ICC(2,1) of 0.86 and mean absolute difference of 6.5%+-5.5% between automated ultrasound-based MP and manual X-ray-based MP; automated measurement took an average of 104 seconds per hip

emb:L2033222110.model_family: various AI systems for X-ray and sonography support (not individually named)
emb:L2033222110.clinical_problem: diagnosis and treatment support for fractures in children and adolescents
emb:L2033222110.patient_population: children and adolescents with suspected fractures in pediatric traumatology
emb:L2033222110.model_description: This narrative overview reviews the current state of AI applications in pediatric traumatology, covering research and development systems and approved medical products that support X-ray and sonographic fracture diagnosis in children and adolescents. It discusses clinical decision support and raises open questions around traceability, explainability, transparency, and trustworthiness specific to this heterogeneous age group.

emb:L2035954266.model_family: 2D convolutional neural network with novel Total Intensity Map input representation
emb:L2035954266.clinical_problem: quantification of visceral and subcutaneous abdominal adipose tissue in children for obesity assessment
emb:L2035954266.model_description: A simple 2D CNN takes novel 'Total Intensity Maps' generated from Dixon-based 3T MRI scans and automatically quantifies abdominal subcutaneous (ASAT) and visceral (VAT) adipose tissue in children, compared against the commercial semi-automated AMRA Researcher tool as the reference/gold standard.
emb:L2035954266.dataset_size: Mexican boys aged 7-9 years (sample size not given numerically)
emb:L2035954266.headline_result: High correlation with AMRA Researcher reference (R2=0.98 for ASAT, R2=0.95 for VAT, both P<1e-11); no significant difference in means (ASAT P=0.1765, VAT P=0.7757); reproducibility coefficients 0.32 L (ASAT) and 0.17 L (VAT)

emb:L2036276241.model_family: deep learning framework with multiscale quality-aware fusion module and clustering-based mix-up (CMX) augmentation
emb:L2036276241.body_region: fetal (general, anatomical structures visualized on prenatal ultrasound)
emb:L2036276241.clinical_problem: automated technical image-quality assessment of fetal ultrasound images
emb:L2036276241.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound, evaluated across five public fetal ultrasound image-quality datasets
emb:L2036276241.model_description: A deep learning framework automatically scores the technical quality of fetal ultrasound images by fusing multi-scale image features, using a clustering-based mix-up strategy to generate additional training samples, and a custom loss function that directly optimizes for global quality-ranking consistency rather than per-image error alone. It was evaluated on five public fetal ultrasound image-quality datasets.
emb:L2036276241.headline_result: The framework outperformed other strong competing methods across all five FUIQA datasets tested (specific numeric metrics not given in the abstract)

emb:L2036311888.model_family: compared FCN-8, FCN-32, U-Net, Inception U-Net, and DeepLabv3+ semantic segmentation networks
emb:L2036311888.clinical_problem: semantic segmentation of hand phalanges on pediatric hand radiographs to support growth and skeletal assessment
emb:L2036311888.patient_population: pediatric subjects, from near-skeletally-mature adolescents to younger children, undergoing hand radiography
emb:L2036311888.model_description: Five deep learning segmentation networks (FCN-8, FCN-32, U-Net, Inception U-Net, DeepLabv3+) were trained and compared to segment individual hand phalanges on radiographs, first using near-skeletally-mature subjects, then testing strategies (synthetic scaling-based augmentation and incremental substitution of real pediatric data) to improve generalization to younger pediatric patients whose bone shapes differ due to ongoing growth.
emb:L2036311888.headline_result: DeepLabv3+ and Inception U-Net performed best on near-skeletally-mature subjects (Mean IoU 0.899 and 0.887); adding 20% real pediatric training data improved Mean IoU by up to 21.1% on pediatric subjects with no adverse effect on near-skeletally-mature performance
